picks.excerpt: Three AI-driven startups (Spain's Alighieria with Publisher OS, Germany's Lit-X, and New Zealand's Narrative Muse) are pitching publishers on data-analytics tools that target different parts of the acquisition and marketing pipeline, promising data can inform decisions long driven by instinct without replacing editorial judgment.
picks.rationale: Concrete new AI tooling that changes how editorial/marketing teams make acquisition decisions — highest actionability and freshest release news, credible trade source.

picks.excerpt: A user discovered that text pasted from Claude into Archive of Our Own retains hidden markup flagging AI involvement, exposing popular fanfiction stories as AI-assisted despite anti-AI tags and dismaying the fan-writing community.
picks.rationale: Actionable craft insight on hidden AI markup and detectability that directly affects how writers handle AI-assisted text; distinct outlet adds source diversity.

picks.excerpt: Audiobook publisher Bolinda used interviews, archival research and human expertise to build an AI-generated voice replicating the late romance author Barbara Cartland, reviving a deceased author's distinctive narration for new audiobook editions.
picks.rationale: Novel AI voice-cloning applied to audiobook narration craft; distinct from the prior Michael Caine/ElevenLabs story, credible trade source.

picks.excerpt: Take-a-Break's Fiction Feast magazine has told regular story contributors that 'AI tools will be used' on future in-house-created stories, signaling how a mass-market short-fiction outlet is changing the way it produces content.
picks.rationale: Fresh signal of AI entering a mass-market fiction production workflow; a concrete change for contributing writers and editors.

dedup_notes.diversity: 4 picks across 3 outlets — The Bookseller x2 (at the <=2 per-outlet cap), Publishers Weekly x1, Jane Friedman x1. All single-category (books), each given a distinct accent from the palette.
dedup_notes.shortfall: Selected 4 vs cap of 5. Fresh candidate pool contained only 4 unique, never-before-seen items after URL/content dedup; all cleared the bar, none padded. Floor 3 met.
